description: Sadaqah: voluntary charity, its reward, every good deed (even a smile) as sadaqah, how it differs from Zakat.

documents.text: Sadaqah is voluntary charity. It has no minimum amount, no fixed rate, no required time, and may be given to anyone in need. The Qur'an encourages it: "The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed [of grain] which grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains." (2:261). "If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you." (2:271).

documents.source_name: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim; Jami' at-Tirmidhi
documents.source_name_ar: صحيح البخاري وصحيح مسلم؛ جامع الترمذي
documents.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6021; Sahih Muslim 1005; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1956
documents.reference_ar: صحيح البخاري 6021؛ صحيح مسلم 1005؛ جامع الترمذي 1956
documents.text: Sadaqah is broader than money. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Every act of goodness is charity (sadaqah)." He also said: "Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity." Sadaqah can therefore be a kind word, help, or any good deed, in addition to voluntary financial giving.
The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Charity does not decrease wealth." Muslims are encouraged to give voluntary charity generously and at any time, beyond the obligatory Zakat.

documents.source_name: MA'NA reviewed concept summary (based on Qur'an 9:60, 2:43, 2:271 and Sahih al-Bukhari 8)
documents.source_name_ar: ملخص مفاهيمي مراجَع من مَعنى (استنادًا إلى التوبة 60، والبقرة 43 و271، وصحيح البخاري 8)
documents.reference_ar: سورة التوبة: 60؛ سورة البقرة: 43؛ سورة البقرة: 271؛ صحيح البخاري 8
documents.text: Zakat and Sadaqah are both forms of giving, but they are not the same. Zakat is obligatory (a pillar of Islam), due only when wealth reaches the nisab and a lunar year passes, paid at a fixed rate (2.5% on savings), and given only to the eight categories named in Qur'an 9:60. Sadaqah is voluntary, has no minimum or fixed rate, can be given at any time, to anyone, and can even be a non-financial good deed. Translating Zakat simply as "charity" can hide this difference, because in many languages "charity" implies something optional. Note that the Qur'an sometimes uses the Arabic word sadaqat for obligatory Zakat (as in 9:60), so the context determines the meaning.
